chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Isa, from Muhammad bin Yahya, the silk maker, from Hammad bin Uthman, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked him about forged statement. He said: From it is the saying of a man to the one who sings: «You did well».
ai.seo_question: What counts as falsehood (qawl al-zur) when praising a singer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this definition of *qawl al-zur* (falsehood) from Imam al-Sadiq, highlighting how social pleasantries like praising a singer can become sinful falsehood if they lack sincerity or truth. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual integrity of everyday speech, where even minor insincerities in entertainment contexts are scrutinized as deviations from truthfulness.
